original_question: Does the collection of known polynomial invariants of degree at most 9 cut out the algebraic variety of 4×4×4 contingency tables (pijk) over C that have tensor rank at most 4, equivalently tables admitting a decomposition pijk = ρAi·σAj·θAk + ρCi·σCj·θCk + ρGi·σGj·θGk + ρTi·σTj·θTk for i, j, k ∈ {A, C, G, T}?
target_in_paper: Section 2, "Graphical Models with Hidden Variables," specifically the "Specific Problem" on page 1, read together with the model definition (2.1) on page 2 and the two families of known invariants in (2.2), (2.3), Propositions 2.1 and 2.2 on pages 3-4. The paper itself says this problem is the one stated in [ASCB, Conjecture 3.24, p. 108]. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the model as 4×4×4 tables indexed by {A,C,G,T}, the rank-at-most-4/tensor-decomposition condition, and the central question about whether the known low-degree invariants determine the model. It also correctly places the problem over C and uses the same decomposition pattern as equation (2.1) in the paper. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper's paper-faithful formulation is ideal-theoretic and homogeneous: it asks about the homogeneous prime ideal of the model, not just informally whether some equations "cut out" the variety. The cited formal version is ASCB Conjecture 3.24: the relevant ideal is conjectured to be generated by homogeneous polynomials of degrees 5 and 9. ([doczz.net](https://doczz.net/doc/8266711/algebraic-statistics-for-computational-biology))

The ambient ring should be made explicit: the homogeneous prime ideal I lives in Q[pAAA, pAAC, ..., pTTT], a polynomial ring in 64 variables; geometrically the variety is considered over C, while statisticians care about the real nonnegative locus. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The paper explicitly disregards the normalization linear form p... - 1 and works with homogeneous equations vanishing on the model. That projective/homogeneous convention is missing from the draft. ([doczz.net](https://doczz.net/doc/8266711/algebraic-statistics-for-computational-biology))

The phrase "known polynomial invariants of degree at most 9" is looser than the paper. The nearby context singles out two specific families only: degree-5 invariants from equation (2.2) and degree-9 invariants from the Strassen construction (2.3). ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

For the degree-5 piece, the paper defines the equations via 3×4×4, 4×3×4, and 4×4×3 subtables using A adj(B) C - C adj(B) A = 0 after clearing denominators; these quintics form the entire degree-5 piece I5, of dimension 1728, with the stated GL(C4)^3-module decomposition in Proposition 2.1. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

For the degree-9 piece, the paper uses 3×3×3 subtables and the numerator of det(A B^{-1} C - C B^{-1} A), the Strassen invariant; Proposition 2.2 says the GL(C4)^3-submodule it generates is not contained in <I5>, has dimension 8000, and is isomorphic to S333(C4) ⊗ S333(C4) ⊗ S333(C4). ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The exact degree restriction should be sharpened from "at most 9" to "degrees 5 and 9," especially because the paper notes that there are no nonzero invariants of degree ≤ 4 in I. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

If the question is to be fully stand-alone in the paper's language, it should say that this is the same model as the naive Bayes model with four classes / the conditional independence model [X1 ⟂⟂ X2 ⟂⟂ X3 | Y] / the general Markov model on K1,3. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let I ⊂ Q[pAAA, pAAC, ..., pTTT] be the homogeneous prime ideal of the Zariski closure in C4 ⊗ C4 ⊗ C4 of the 4×4×4 tables (pijk), indexed by i,j,k ∈ {A,C,G,T}, that admit a decomposition pijk = ρAiσAjθAk + ρCiσCjθCk + ρGiσGjθGk + ρTiσTjθTk. Disregarding the normalization linear form p... - 1, is I generated by the known homogeneous invariants of degrees 5 and 9—namely the GL(C4)^3-translates of the quintics obtained from A adj(B) C - C adj(B) A = 0 on 3×4×4 subtables, together with the degree-9 Strassen invariants obtained as the numerators of det(A B^{-1} C - C B^{-1} A) on 3×3×3 subtables? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for the naive Bayes model with four classes—also described in the paper as the conditional independence model [X1 ⟂⟂ X2 ⟂⟂ X3 | Y] and the general Markov model on the three-leaf tree K1,3—is the homogeneous prime ideal generated by the known degree-5 and degree-9 invariants? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is close to the paper's first concrete open problem, but the nearest official formulation is stronger and sharper than "cut out the variety." In Section 2 the paper first poses the specific problem using the language of degree-5 and degree-9 invariants, then defines the model and its homogeneous prime ideal I, and then identifies the two known families of invariants via equations (2.2) and (2.3) and Propositions 2.1 and 2.2. Most importantly, the paper explicitly points to ASCB Conjecture 3.24, whose formal statement is that the relevant homogeneous ideal is generated by polynomials of degrees 5 and 9. So the refined version replaces the draft's set-theoretic wording by the paper-faithful ideal-generation question, while preserving your model and decomposition essentially unchanged. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
